@@ -0,0 +1,30 @@
+from __future__ import (absolute_import, division, print_function)
+__metaclass__ = type
+
+import pytest
+
+from ansible.module_utils.facts.hardware.freebsd import FreeBSDHardware
+from ansible.module_utils.facts.hardware.netbsd import NetBSDHardware
+from ansible.module_utils.facts.hardware.openbsd import OpenBSDHardware
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize('hardware_class,method_names', [
+    (FreeBSDHardware, ('get_cpu_facts', 'get_memory_facts', 'get_dmi_facts', 'get_device_facts', 'get_mount_facts')),
+    (NetBSDHardware, ('get_cpu_facts', 'get_memory_facts', 'get_dmi_facts', 'get_mount_facts')),
+    (OpenBSDHardware, ('get_processor_facts', 'get_memory_facts', 'get_dmi_facts', 'get_device_facts', 'get_mount_facts')),
+])
+def test_bsd_populate_merges_uptime_with_other_facts(mocker, hardware_class, method_names):
+    module = mocker.Mock()
+    module.get_bin_path.return_value = '/sbin/sysctl'
+    module.run_command.return_value = (0, '100', '')
+    mocker.patch('ansible.module_utils.facts.sysctl.time.time', return_value=150)
+    hardware = hardware_class(module)
+    for method_name in method_names:
+        mocker.patch.object(hardware, method_name, return_value={method_name: method_name})
+    if hardware_class is not FreeBSDHardware:
+        mocker.patch('ansible.module_utils.facts.hardware.%s.get_sysctl' % hardware_class.platform.lower(), return_value={})
+
+    facts = hardware.populate()
+    assert facts['uptime_seconds'] == 50
+    for method_name in method_names:
+        assert facts[method_name] == method_name

@@ -0,0 +1,92 @@
+from __future__ import (absolute_import, division, print_function)
+__metaclass__ = type
+
+import errno
+
+import pytest
+
+from ansible.module_utils.facts.sysctl import get_sysctl, get_uptime_facts
+
+
+def test_sysctl_parses_platform_delimiters_and_continuations(mocker):
+    module = mocker.Mock()
+    module.get_bin_path.return_value = '/sbin/sysctl'
+    module.run_command.return_value = (0, 'hw.ncpu=4\nkern.name: OpenBSD\nvm.swappiness 60\ninvalid\nkern.text: first\n  second\n\n  fourth\nthird\n', '')
+
+    assert get_sysctl(module, ['hw', 'kern']) == {
+        'hw.ncpu': '4', 'kern.name': 'OpenBSD', 'vm.swappiness': '60',
+        'kern.text': 'first\n  second\n\n  fourth',
+    }
+    assert module.warn.call_count == 2
+    assert module.warn.call_args_list[0][0][0].startswith('Unable to split sysctl line (invalid): ')
+    assert module.warn.call_args_list[1][0][0].startswith('Unable to split sysctl line (third): ')
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize('failure,warning', [
+    ((1, '', 'permission denied'), 'Unable to read sysctl: permission denied'),
+    (IOError('read failed'), 'Unable to read sysctl: read failed'),
+])
+def test_sysctl_command_failure(mocker, failure, warning):
+    module = mocker.Mock()
+    module.get_bin_path.return_value = '/sbin/sysctl'
+    if isinstance(failure, tuple):
+        module.run_command.return_value = failure
+    else:
+        module.run_command.side_effect = failure
+    assert get_sysctl(module, ['hw']) == {}
+    module.warn.assert_called_once_with(warning)
+
+
+def test_missing_sysctl_raises(mocker):
+    module = mocker.Mock()
+    module.get_bin_path.return_value = None
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
+        get_sysctl(module, ['hw'])
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
+        get_uptime_facts(module)
+
+    module.run_command.side_effect = None
+    module.get_bin_path.side_effect = OSError(errno.ENOENT, 'missing')
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
+        get_sysctl(module, ['hw'])
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
+        get_uptime_facts(module)
+
+    module.get_bin_path.side_effect = None
+    module.get_bin_path.return_value = '/sbin/sysctl'
+    module.run_command.side_effect = OSError(errno.ENOENT, 'missing')
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
+        get_sysctl(module, ['hw'])
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
+        get_uptime_facts(module)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize('output,expected', [
+    ('100\n', {'uptime_seconds': 50}),
+    ('100.5', {'uptime_seconds': 49}),
+    ('', {}),
+    ('{ sec = 100, usec = 0 }', {}),
+    ('not-a-number', {}),
+])
+def test_uptime_uses_only_numeric_boot_time(mocker, output, expected):
+    module = mocker.Mock()
+    module.get_bin_path.return_value = '/sbin/sysctl'
+    module.run_command.return_value = (0, output, '')
+    mocker.patch('ansible.module_utils.facts.sysctl.time.time', return_value=150)
+    assert get_uptime_facts(module) == expected
+    module.run_command.assert_called_once_with(['/sbin/sysctl', '-n', 'kern.boottime'])
+
+
+def test_uptime_command_failure(mocker):
+    module = mocker.Mock()
+    module.get_bin_path.return_value = '/sbin/sysctl'
+    module.run_command.return_value = (1, '', 'unavailable')
+    assert get_uptime_facts(module) == {}
+    module.warn.assert_called_once_with('Unable to read sysctl: unavailable')
+
+
+def test_sysctl_binary_lookup_ioerror_warns(mocker):
+    module = mocker.Mock()
+    module.get_bin_path.side_effect = IOError('lookup failed')
+    assert get_sysctl(module, ['hw']) == {}
+    module.warn.assert_called_once_with('Unable to read sysctl: lookup failed')

+from ansible.module_utils.facts.sysctl import get_sysctl, get_uptime_facts
+
+
+def test_sysctl_parses_platform_delimiters_and_continuations(mocker):
+    module = mocker.Mock()
+    module.get_bin_path.return_value = '/sbin/sysctl'
+    module.run_command.return_value = (0, 'hw.ncpu=4\nkern.name: OpenBSD\nvm.swappiness 60\ninvalid\nkern.text: first\n  second\n\n  fourth\nthird\n', '')
+
+    assert get_sysctl(module, ['hw', 'kern']) == {
+        'hw.ncpu': '4', 'kern.name': 'OpenBSD', 'vm.swappiness': '60',
+        'kern.text': 'first\n  second\n\n  fourth',
+    }
+    assert module.warn.call_count == 2
+    assert module.warn.call_args_list[0][0][0].startswith('Unable to split sysctl line (invalid): ')
+    assert module.warn.call_args_list[1][0][0].startswith('Unable to split sysctl line (third): ')
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize('failure,warning', [
+    ((1, '', 'permission denied'), 'Unable to read sysctl: permission denied'),
+    (IOError('read failed'), 'Unable to read sysctl: read failed'),
+])
+def test_sysctl_command_failure(mocker, failure, warning):
+    module = mocker.Mock()
+    module.get_bin_path.return_value = '/sbin/sysctl'
+    if isinstance(failure, tuple):
+        module.run_command.return_value = failure
+    else:
+        module.run_command.side_effect = failure
+    assert get_sysctl(module, ['hw']) == {}
+    module.warn.assert_called_once_with(warning)
+
+
+def test_missing_sysctl_raises(mocker):
+    module = mocker.Mock()
+    module.get_bin_path.return_value = None
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
+        get_sysctl(module, ['hw'])
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
+        get_uptime_facts(module)
+
+    module.run_command.side_effect = None
+    module.get_bin_path.side_effect = OSError(errno.ENOENT, 'missing')
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
+        get_sysctl(module, ['hw'])
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
+        get_uptime_facts(module)
+
+    module.get_bin_path.side_effect = None
+    module.get_bin_path.return_value = '/sbin/sysctl'
+    module.run_command.side_effect = OSError(errno.ENOENT, 'missing')
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
+        get_sysctl(module, ['hw'])
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
+        get_uptime_facts(module)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize('output,expected', [
+    ('100\n', {'uptime_seconds': 50}),
+    ('100.5', {'uptime_seconds': 49}),
+    ('', {}),
+    ('{ sec = 100, usec = 0 }', {}),
+    ('not-a-number', {}),
+])
+def test_uptime_uses_only_numeric_boot_time(mocker, output, expected):
+    module = mocker.Mock()
+    module.get_bin_path.return_value = '/sbin/sysctl'
+    module.run_command.return_value = (0, output, '')
+    mocker.patch('ansible.module_utils.facts.sysctl.time.time', return_value=150)
+    assert get_uptime_facts(module) == expected
+    module.run_command.assert_called_once_with(['/sbin/sysctl', '-n', 'kern.boottime'])
+
+
+def test_uptime_command_failure(mocker):
+    module = mocker.Mock()
+    module.get_bin_path.return_value = '/sbin/sysctl'
+    module.run_command.return_value = (1, '', 'unavailable')
+    assert get_uptime_facts(module) == {}
+    module.warn.assert_called_once_with('Unable to read sysctl: unavailable')
+
+
+def test_sysctl_binary_lookup_ioerror_warns(mocker):
+    module = mocker.Mock()
+    module.get_bin_path.side_effect = IOError('lookup failed')
+    assert get_sysctl(module, ['hw']) == {}
+    module.warn.assert_called_once_with('Unable to read sysctl: lookup failed')
